The profile shows the cost is in world.query and per-component get() lookups, which now happen three times per entity per frame, plus rebuilding the grid every frame. reference.summary: Attempted to split a large game world update loop into separate entity-component-system modules for movement and collision. Tests passed but mean frame time rose from about 11 to about 20 ms, profiling traced it to repeated component queries and per-frame grid rebuilds, and the change was reverted before a demo with the benchmark back to baseline.
facts: Baseline benchmark was about 11.2 ms mean per frame
After the split tests passed but mean frame time rose to 19.7 ms
Profiling pointed at world.query, per-component get lookups and grid rebuilds
The refactor was reverted and the benchmark returned to about 11.3 ms
Cached queries or archetype storage were noted as needed for a later attempt

decisions.choice: Revert the refactor instead of optimising it now
decisions.reason: the demo build ships the next day
